summary.headline: HEG Q4 FY26 net loss of INR 189 crore on unrealised GrafTech fair-value and FX losses; operating EBITDA margin ~19% with sales volume down ~1,000 tons QoQ.
summary.overview: HEG reported FY26 revenue growth with sales volume up 20% YoY, EBITDA of INR 497 crore (19% margin) in Q4 versus INR 388 crore a year earlier, and FY PBT of INR 246 crore (up 66%). The quarter was hit by a net loss of INR 189 crore, which management attributes to unrealised fair-value losses on its GrafTech investment and an approximately 5% rupee depreciation within the quarter, with the FX loss estimated at INR 35-40 crore. Q4 sales volume fell about 1,000 tons QoQ as Middle East orders were postponed due to the conflict and a lower-priced regional mix weighed on realisations. Management signalled price increases for unbooked orders from H2 and guided EBITDA margin of about 20% for Q1 and Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: Up 20% YoY for the year; Q4 down ~1,000 tons QoQ

segments.name: Graphite electrodes (HEG core)
segments.commentary: Capacity of 100,000 tons after expansion from 80,000; utilisation above 90% for the full year and about 95% on production basis in Q4, with sales-side utilisation lower. Around 70% of output exported to 30-40 countries; MENA about 20% of annual sales.

segments.name: HEG Greentech / TACC (battery materials)
segments.commentary: Pilot plant for sampling set up 18+ months ago; sampling underway with Indian cell makers and LG, Panasonic, CATL. Plant commissioning date unchanged from April; first-year utilisation expected at 40-60%.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected around 20% for Q1 and Q2 FY27 per CFO; management said committed-volume quarters could land nearer 17-18%.
Full-year FY27 EBITDA margin guided to be more than 20% (CFO, on call).
Price increases to be pursued on unbooked orders from H2 FY27; quantum (300/400/500 per ton range mentioned) not yet determinable.
Expansion from 100,000 to 115,000 tons targeted for early 2028.
Composite scheme of arrangement with GrafTech progressing; NCLT approval anticipated in Q2 FY27 subject to approvals.
Rupee-related FX loss expected to reverse if rupee appreciates, with some reversal possible next quarter.
capex_capacity: Electrode capacity 100,000 tons after recent expansion from 80,000 tons; next expansion of 15,000 tons to 115,000 tons under construction, target early 2028.
Near Bhopal plant described as the largest single-site graphite electrode plant globally at 100,000 tons.
HEG Greentech/TACC: plant commissioning on schedule from April 2026; sampling with OEMs ongoing.
Needle coke covered for purchases through end-June shipments, which safely covers costs until September; power, other raw materials and energy not hedged.
demand_pricing: Management expects about 200,000 tons of incremental electrode demand by 2030 ex-China from EAF capacity additions (about 100 million tons of new EAF capacity globally ex-China).
Orders booked three to six months ahead; booked up to about September; new inquiries being priced higher, with price increases offered on uncommitted volumes.
Q4 realisation dip attributed to a lower-priced regional and order mix, expected to reverse in April-June.
Middle East customers facing disruption; some buyers willing to pay USD 200-300 per ton extra for road freight, per management.
Management said GrafTech announced price increases of USD 600-1,200 per ton; HEG's own quantum not yet fixed.
Competition: management argues Chinese UHP exports are limited (about 100,000 of 400,000 tons exported) and that HEG is the lowest-cost producer.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike is being targeted from this FY and is there a needle coke cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish Gulati said booked orders run to about September and unbooked orders will see increases from H2; quantum varies by region and cannot yet be sized. Energy and freight costs have already risen, and a lag exists because product takes about two months to make and ship.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue low in Q4 - volume or realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was about 1,000 tons lower and price dipped due to regional and order mix; the effect was described as temporary and expected to reverse in April-June. It dented operating profit.

qa_highlights.question: Is HEG covered on needle coke costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Needle coke is covered for shipments from origin through end-June, which with about 45 days transit and 45 days processing protects costs until September. Other raw materials and energy are not covered.

qa_highlights.question: Has there been force majeure or price renegotiation under contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Force majeure letters were sent for Middle East orders where freight rose from USD 20-30 to over USD 300 per ton; customers pay the extra freight on FOB Mumbai terms. Freight increases for US and Europe have been absorbable so far.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 loss is from GrafTech and FX, and is there a shipping hit in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the FX loss is unrealised and estimated at INR 35-40 crore; other expenses also include the fair-value loss, which is why other expenses rose QoQ. Other income fell because fair-value losses were classified in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 utilisation and volume not reconcile with Q3 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Production-based utilisation was about 95% in Q4 and above 90% for FY; sales volume was about 1,000 tons lower QoQ, reflecting postponed orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA guidance given Q3 indicated ~22%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said margin should be about 20% for Q1 and Q2 FY27, with full-year above 20%. Management also said committed-volume quarters could be around 17-18%.

risks_watch: Middle East disruption (Hormuz) delaying about 20% of annual sales, with postponed orders to ship once normalised.
Needle coke and energy cost pass-through after September, given no contract cover beyond needle coke and rising crude-linked inputs.
US anti-dumping/countervailing duty outcome on Indian and Chinese electrodes expected in roughly four to five months; EU tariff-rate quota from 1 July 2026.
Unrealised GrafTech investment losses and rupee moves continuing to distort reported PAT; reversal depends on rupee and GrafTech share price.
Whether announced price increases stick given peer behaviour and customer acceptance; no formal price quantum yet.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term EAF demand and cost leadership, but cautious and somewhat evasive on near-term pricing quantum, needle coke outlook and US duty outcomes, repeatedly deferring specifics ("we can take it offline"). Management was defensive about the GrafTech investment, reaffirming it as a long-term bet.
key_quotes: And we are very well placed to meet some of this new demand with our recent expansion from 80,000 to 100,000 tons.
But definitely towards H2, our aim is to have price increase, not only to protect our margins, but to help improve further.
We remain fully committed to this investment, and we are confident in the long-term value it will create for our stakeholders.
So, they have to explain to their stakeholders why they are at this.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin above 20% and price increases on unbooked H2 orders, backed by booked orders three to six months ahead and the 100k t capacity now running at ~95% production utilisation; the 115k t expansion targets early 2028 with Q1-Q2 FY27 margin guidance cut to ~17-18% on committed volumes.
